claim:
Let \(C\sim\operatorname{LKJ}_n(\eta)\) with \(n\ge 3\), \(\eta>0\), and \(
u=n+2\eta-1\). For any three distinct off-diagonal entries, \(\mathbb E[C_{e_1}C_{e_2}C_{e_3}]=
u^{-2}\) exactly when the three unordered edges form one triangle, and the expectation is \(0\) otherwise. Consequently the off-diagonal entries, although pairwise independent, are not three-wise independent, and \(\mathbb E\,\operatorname{tr}((C-I_n)^3)=n(n-1)(n-2)/
u^2\). If \(\eta_n/n	o	heta\in[0,\infty)\), then \(n^{-1}\mathbb E\,\operatorname{tr}((C-I_n)^3)	o(1+2	heta)^{-2}\), the third centered moment of the corresponding Marchenko--Pastur limit.

correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the \(3\times3\) LKJ conditional density exactly, proves its center is \(C_{12}C_{13}\), uses the published pairwise-independence theorem and exact second moment \(1/(n+2\eta-1)\), and separately handles every nontriangle by diagonal-sign symmetry. The cubic trace is then an exact count of ordered triangles. No finite simulation is used as proof.

value.rationale: The motivating source makes higher-order dependence the precise structural gap left after pairwise independence. The exact triangle cumulant identifies the first obstruction, localizes it graphically, and yields an exact cubic spectral moment that matches the third centered moment of the limiting Marchenko--Pastur law. This is a natural finite-dimensional statistic with direct use in network and spectral interpretations, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
